meta.title: Chokepoint
meta.subtitle: A reverse stress test of an AI chip
meta.disclaimer: Illustrative teaching model · TTS / TTR weeks are invented to teach the method, not forecasts · real-world facts are sourced and dated
meta.rules: A card stops a node for its TTR weeks. Two cards on the same node add up. If any critical node's TTR is longer than its TTS, the chip is CHOKED.
meta.method: Time-to-Survive / Time-to-Recover after Simchi-Levi et al. (HBR 2014; Interfaces 2015).

nodes.label: High-purity quartz
nodes.why: Ultra-pure quartz sand is melted into crucibles.

nodes.label: Quartz crucibles
nodes.why: Crucibles hold molten silicon while ingots are pulled. Consumed every run.

nodes.label: Silicon wafers
nodes.why: Ingots are sliced and polished into 300 mm wafers.

nodes.label: EUV lithography
nodes.why: Only EUV scanners can print the smallest transistor layers.

nodes.label: Neon gas
nodes.why: Purified neon feeds the lasers in DUV lithography.

nodes.label: Photoresist
nodes.why: Light-sensitive chemical that holds the circuit pattern. Short shelf life.

nodes.label: Gallium & germanium
nodes.why: Minor metals used in power chips, optics and fab process steps.

nodes.label: Advanced fab
nodes.why: Where the AI logic die is actually made.

nodes.label: HBM memory
nodes.why: Stacked high-bandwidth memory sits next to the AI die.

nodes.label: Advanced packaging
nodes.why: Die + HBM are bonded on one interposer (CoWoS-type).

nodes.label: Tantalum capacitors
nodes.why: Coltan becomes tantalum, used in tiny capacitors on the board.

nodes.label: Rare-earth magnets
nodes.why: Magnets for server fans, drives and cooling pumps.

nodes.label: Solar power
nodes.why: Panels that partly power the data center.

nodes.label: AI data center
nodes.why: Where the finished chip goes to work.

cards.title: Taiwan Strait blockade

cards.title: US forced-labour detention order
cards.blurb: Customs detains solar panels under the UFLPA.

cards.title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse / M23
cards.blurb: A landslide at an armed-group-controlled coltan mine.

cards.title: Dutch export rule on lithography
cards.blurb: Licence rules tighten on ASML tools, slowing servicing and spare parts.

cards.title: Neon plant shelled
cards.blurb: A neon purification plant goes offline.

cards.title: Japan earthquake
cards.blurb: Wafer and chemical plants halt for safety checks.

cards.title: Ransomware on a wafer maker
cards.blurb: Factory systems are encrypted and production stops. (Hypothetical, based on a real 2023 attack on a chip-equipment supplier.)

fixes.label: Stockpile 3 months of crucibles
fixes.who_pays: Your shareholders (cash tied up in inventory).

fixes.label: Qualify a second wafer supplier
fixes.ethics_note: Neutral. Spreads orders across more plants.

fixes.label: Neon recycling at the fab
fixes.ethics_note: Uses less gas and depends less on a war zone.
fixes.who_pays: Nobody much. Capital cost up front.

fixes.label: Stockpile cheap rare earths (Myanmar-linked)
fixes.ethics_note: Cheapest feedstock is linked to militia-run mines in Kachin State, Myanmar.
fixes.who_pays: Kachin communities: polluted water, landslides, armed control.

fixes.label: Second magnet supplier outside China
fixes.ethics_note: Traceable non-China supply, at a premium.
fixes.who_pays: You: about 4x the cost of the Myanmar stockpile.

fixes.label: Buy coltan from any source, no questions
fixes.ethics_note: Untraced coltan from eastern DRC can finance armed groups.
fixes.who_pays: Congolese miners and communities under armed-group control.

fixes.label: Conflict-minerals audit (certified smelters)
fixes.who_pays: You: audits and a slower, smaller supplier pool.

fixes.label: Redesign: replace tantalum capacitors
fixes.who_pays: Engineers, plus a 6-month board redesign delay.

fixes.label: Traced, non-Xinjiang solar panels
fixes.ethics_note: Avoids forced-labour risk and customs detentions.

fixes.label: Pre-buy 6 months of AI chips
fixes.ethics_note: Hoarding starves smaller buyers such as universities, start-ups and hospitals.
fixes.who_pays: Smaller buyers priced out of scarce chips.

fixes.label: Build a leading-edge fab outside Taiwan
fixes.ethics_note: The real fix for Taiwan risk, and far beyond a $10M budget.

break: Say: 'Normal stress tests ask what if. We start from the failure: no AI chip ships. Your job is to break the chain with the FEWEST cards.'
Let the class call out cards. Point at the countdown: each node has weeks of inventory (TTS). If recovery (TTR) takes longer, the chip is choked.
After the CHOKED stamp, ask: 'Was that the smallest set? Could one card do it?' Reveal par, then press 2.
fix: Say: 'You have $10M. Buy fixes. Some are cheap. Watch the ethics column.'
Let the class pick fixes, then press REPLAY to rerun the same cards. Green = survived, red = still choked.
Point out that no affordable fix stops the Taiwan card. Some chokepoints can't be bought away. Press 3.
judge: Read the two meters out loud: Resilience (share of 1- and 2-card attacks the chain now survives) vs Ethics.
Click through the 'who pays' lines. Ask who in the room would sign off on the Myanmar stockpile.
End on the question: 'Who pays for your resilience?' Let it sit for 10 seconds.

facts.text: USGS: two companies near Spruce Pine, NC produce US high-purity quartz; the US is estimated world leader in HPQ production.
USGS: no economic substitutes exist for high-purity quartz in most applications; Spruce Pine HPQ exceeds 99.999% purity.
High-purity quartz is made into fused quartz crucibles used to grow silicon ingots that are sliced into semiconductor and solar wafers.
Quartz crucibles used in Czochralski silicon pulling erode and deform at over 1,400°C, limiting their life; they are a consumable.
Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical and SUMCO together account for roughly half of the global silicon wafer market.
ASML (Netherlands) is the only maker of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment used for the most advanced AI chips.
facts.source_name: Reuters (via The Star), Max A. Cherney

facts.text: Ukraine's Ingas (Mariupol) and Cryoin (Odesa) supplied an estimated 45–54% of the world's semiconductor-grade neon before 2022.
Japanese firms such as JSR and Tokyo Ohka Kogyo hold about 90% of the global photoresist market, per the US trade agency.
facts.source_name: US International Trade Administration – Japan Country Commercial Guide: Semiconductors

facts.text: By some estimates, TSMC produces over 90% of the world's most advanced chips.
SK hynix (50%) and Samsung (33%) held most HBM market share in Q2 2026; US-based Micron held 18%.
facts.source_name: Counterpoint Research – Global DRAM and HBM Market Share

facts.text: TSMC's chairman said in 2023 the AI chip shortage stemmed from CoWoS packaging capacity, meeting only about 80% of demand.
facts.source_name: The Register (relaying Nikkei Asia interview with Mark Liu)

facts.text: USGS: China accounted for 99% of world primary low-purity gallium production.
USGS: China remained the leading global producer and exporter of germanium metal in 2025; global data are limited.
USGS estimates Congo (Kinshasa) mined about 1,300 t of tantalum in 2025, roughly half the world total; Rwanda ranked second (400 t).
Dodd-Frank Section 1502 conflict minerals rules cover tantalum, tin, gold and tungsten (3TG).
facts.source_name: US SEC – Conflict Minerals fact sheet

facts.text: EU Conflict Minerals Regulation (EU) 2017/821 covers tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold; importer duties apply from 1 January 2021.
China accounts for about 94% of global sintered NdFeB permanent magnet production.
facts.source_name: Columbia University Center on Global Energy Policy

facts.text: Global Witness: Myanmar is the largest source of heavy rare earths; Kachin mining sites are controlled by military-aligned militias.
facts.source_name: Global Witness – Fuelling the future, poisoning the present

facts.text: US data centers used about 4.4% of US electricity in 2023; LBNL projects 6.7–12% by 2028.
facts.source_name: US Department of Energy (LBNL 2024 Data Center Energy Usage Report)

facts.text: IEA: China's Xinjiang province accounts for 40% of global polysilicon manufacturing.
facts.source_name: Utility Dive (quoting IEA Special Report on Solar PV Global Supply Chains)

facts.text: Under UFLPA, CBP presumes goods made wholly or partly in Xinjiang are made with forced labour and barred, unless rebutted.
facts.source_name: US Customs and Border Protection – UFLPA

facts.text: Sibelco and The Quartz Corp halted Spruce Pine operations from 26 Sept 2024 after Hurricane Helene; Sibelco restarted about two weeks later.
China imposed gallium export licensing in Aug 2023, banned exports to the US in Dec 2024, and lifted that ban for one year in Nov 2025.
facts.source_name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 – Gallium / Germanium

facts.text: China suspended its gallium, germanium and antimony export ban to the US from 9 Nov 2025 until 27 Nov 2026; licensing still applies.
China's 'Justice Mission 2025' drills (29–30 Dec 2025) simulated a blockade of Taiwan and its main ports, Keelung and Kaohsiung.
UFLPA's rebuttable presumption took effect 21 June 2022, barring Xinjiang-linked goods unless importers rebut it.
facts.source_name: US Customs and Border Protection – UFLPA

facts.text: CBP told Reuters it had detained 1,053 solar equipment shipments under UFLPA from 21 June to 25 Oct 2022.
UN experts reported M23 seized Rubaya in April 2024 and collected at least $800,000 a month from coltan levies.
facts.source_name: Reuters (Sonia Rolley, Alessandra Prentice), via Kitco

facts.text: A landslide at Rubaya coltan mines (28 Jan 2026) killed over 200, per rebel-appointed officials; Rubaya produces ~15% of world coltan.
A second Rubaya landslide on 3 Mar 2026 killed over 200, per DRC's mines minister; M23 disputed the toll.
From 1 Sep 2023, Dutch rules required export licences for ASML's TWINSCAN NXT:2000i and later immersion DUV systems.
From 7 Sep 2024, the Netherlands also required Dutch licences for ASML NXT:1970i and 1980i DUV systems; EUV sales already needed licences.
After Russia's 2022 invasion, Ingas (Mariupol) and Cryoin (Odesa) halted neon production; Cryoin stopped on 24 Feb 2022.
The 16 Mar 2022 Fukushima-offshore earthquake halted production at Renesas' Naka, Takasaki and Yonezawa chip plants.
DRC banned trade in minerals from 38 artisanal sites in North and South Kivu, including tantalum ore, extending it six months in Nov 2025.
Chip-equipment supplier MKS Instruments disclosed a ransomware event on 3 Feb 2023 and suspended operations at some facilities.
Simchi-Levi, Schmidt & Wei (HBR, Jan–Feb 2014) measure risk by each node's time to recover (TTR), not by disruption probability.
Simchi-Levi et al. (Interfaces, 2015) define time-to-survive as the longest a firm can last without losing demand after a disruption.
